thread:
maria: heads-up — we're seeing a big spike in evictions in us-west2 spot pools and 99th pct latency is climbing for gen-heavy routes. Not sure if it's a single AZ or wider. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: alert triggered: GpuNodeEvictionRate > 20% in us-west2 over last 5m. Affected pools: spot-gpu-a, spot-gpu-b. Alert links: https://ops.redwood/alerts/1770001111
sam: looking at prometheus — evictions_count{pool=~\"spot-gpu.*\",region=\"us-west2\"} spiked ~3x starting 1770000900. Also see scheduling failures in kube: `FailedScheduling` for pods waiting on nvidia.com/gpu.
diego: any sign of preemption messages from cloud provider? I want the instance ids. Can we correlate with last maintenance window?
maria: cloud-sre-bot posted a preemption bulletin: "Spot capacity reduced due to maintenance in us-west2-a and us-west2-c". Instance IDs in events: i-0a123..., i-0b456..., i-0c789...
lia: quick note — traffic to gen endpoints is pinned to model-version-prod-3.0 which requires 24GB GPU. We have cheaper 16GB instances in mixed pool but can't run without model sharding.
sam: chart: request latency (p95/p99) for /v1/generate — p99 jumped from 180ms -> 1.4s. Throughput dropped ~18%. Here is the prometheus query I ran: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=\"/v1/generate\"}[5m])) by (le))`
maria: we've already retried some requests; clients see errors `503` from the gateway because pods didn't come up fast enough. first priority: stop user-facing errors. second: minimize spend.
diego: mitigation options: 1) failover some gen traffic to dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) 2) temporarily uplist some ondemand instances in us-west2 3) spin up smaller-quantized model variants on 16GB nodes as a fallback.
lia: option 3 needs a short canary eval but could reduce latency and cost — quantized v3-small has slightly worse quality but will keep availability. We can route, e.g., 20% traffic to v3-small immediately.
sam: operational steps I suggest: - increase deployment max surge for gen-prod to allow rapid pod creation - adjust cluster-autoscaler to prefer on-demand for next 10m - add dynamic routing rule to send 20% to v3-small
maria: can someone run the autoscaler tweak? Command to patch: `kubectl patch configmap cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --type merge -p '{"data":{"preferOnDemand":"true"}}'`
k8s-deploy-bot: rollout start confirmed for deployment gen-prod at 1770001205. Patch applied: preferOnDemand=true.
diego: I'm spinning up 4 on-demand gpus in us-west2 via `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-v100,count=1 --preemptible=false` — will attach to dedicated-gpu-ng pool. ETA ~5m.
ops-bot: provisioning events: 4 on-demand nodes requested, 2 active in us-west2-b at 1770001298. Autoscaler still reconciling.
sam: routing rule applied: 20% to v3-small canary via the gateway config. Snippet: ```
route:
  - match: {path_prefix: "/v1/generate"}
    weighted_backends:
      - backend: gen-prod-v3
        weight: 80
      - backend: gen-prod-v3-small
        weight: 20
```
lia: can we also enable KV cache warmup for the small model to avoid cold-start latency? I ran a quick warmup script: `python infra/warmup.py --model v3-small --prefixes 500`
maria: warmup looks good. p50/p95 for small canary ~210ms/380ms. Production p99 still high but trending down as on-demand nodes come up.
cloud-finance: quick cost note — if we keep the 4 on-demand V100s for 24h it's roughly +$3.6k/day. If we bounce to more quantized smalls, it's more CPU-heavy but cheaper. Confirming we should proceed?
diego: yes proceed — prioritize availability. We'll evaluate next 12h and decide whether to commit reserved capacity or rely on mixed pools with better fallback.
maria: after autoscaler pref change and 4 on-demand up, evictions dropped to normal levels and p99 down to ~260ms at 1770001500. We'll keep the canary at 20% and increase to 50% only if errors reappear.
sam: follow-ups: 1) add an automated policy to prefer on-demand for 10m after eviction rate > 15% 2) add a placement rule to prefer spreading across AZs to avoid correlated maintenance 3) add a precomputed quantized fallback for all prod models
lia: I'll own (3) — start export & quantization pipeline, ETA 2d.
cloud-finance: I'll model the 30-day cost of keeping a small reserved pool (4x 24GB GPUs) vs on-demand spikes and post a recommendation.
maria: thanks team. Logging action: created incident ticket INC-1770001 and added runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/spot-preemptive-failover. Marking P1 mitigated, monitoring.
